The gate that produced that statement reads telemetry only, and the network channel was itself broken on that date.

claims.title: In Enforce the whole telemetry layer is worth 0.0009, and one attack class is indistinguishable from benign traffic
claims.statement: Three predictions were written before the measurement. The two security modes are mirrors: Permissive loses 0.299 to telemetry-zeroing and 0.072 to network-zeroing, Enforce loses 0.001 and 0.302. The eighteen-column telemetry layer is therefore worth 0.0009 under Enforce, which deepens the earlier finding that eight classes had no exclusive signal: the problem is not those eight classes but the whole channel. Scanning all 138 non-constant aggregate columns, `hmac_forgery` reaches a maximum separability against `normal` of 0.0507 out of a theoretical 0.5, against 0.5000 for `service_dos` and 0.4994 for `confused_deputy`. The defence still stopped it: eleven forgeries rejected, zero accepted, the next genuine message delivered.

claims.title: The core argument now has a quantitative form, a scope boundary, and three pre-registered attempts
claims.statement: Three measures of per-class separability were each pre-registered in its own commit before being computed, and each was correlated against the sealed-holdout per-class recall. X_old (maximum separability against `normal`) gives Spearman +0.3344 for Permissive, not significant, and +0.6334 for Enforce at p<.01. X_new (minimum separability against the nearest attack neighbour) gives +0.4001 and +0.5968. Their minimum gives +0.7139 at p<.01 for Enforce, the highest in this project, and a control shows the entire +0.1171 gain comes from one class changing places. The third variant, a directional read-out, was falsified: Permissive flips sign to -0.4137. The boundary is explicit: the relationship holds only where the binary task has not saturated.

claims.title: The single-batch ceiling is not a Permissive-only property, and one of my own statistics was wrong
claims.statement: Restricting the large dataset to a single three-hour window reproduces the small dataset's class geometry in Enforce as well: ratio 1.9983 against 1.9234, a relative difference of 3.9%. After controlling for class count the collapse factor is 3.7552 for Enforce against 3.6622 for Permissive, a 2.5% difference, so the batch effect is the same size in both modes. The same round corrected an earlier statement of mine: the figure that the forest beats nearest-neighbour by only 0.045 compared an unbalanced 1-NN score with a balanced forest score. The correct value is +0.1292, so choosing a learner is worth 0.02 while having one is worth 0.13 to 0.16.

claims.title: Under Enforce the adaptive attacker could not adapt, and that is the defence working
claims.statement: Answering a labelling question with existing data required checking the instrument, and the check found something larger. Excluding sessions already recorded as blind, all 9,196 Enforce bursts show zero velocity signal and zero alerts, 1,359 of 1,359 Enforce sessions carry no signal on either channel for their whole duration, and 100.0% of decisions are the single branch 'not noticed, so escalate'. The mechanism is that the observer runs without a keystore, so under Enforce its subscription is created but no protected publisher pairs with it. This extends the earlier count of 113 blind sessions to 1,829, and the new group is recorded by the program as having a healthy observer. The labelling question itself was answered by the pre-registered rule: do not change the label.

claims.title: Binary detection has a one-time holdout number, obtained by folding a published product
claims.statement: The sealed-holdout confusion matrices were already on disk as full 18x18 and 20x20 tables whose row sums equal the per-class holdout session counts. Coarsening them to binary required no model to be rerun and no row of test to be read again. Permissive is 242 of 242 correct, with 197 true positives, zero false negatives, zero false positives and 45 true negatives. Enforce is 227/20/4/41, giving recall 0.9190, false alarm 0.0889 and balanced accuracy 0.9151. Both carry independent_final_test true. This is also the first time the project's central asymmetry has been measured on one one-time dataset: binary 1.0000 and 0.9151 against identification 0.4655 and 0.4228. That number had been computable for six weeks and nobody had folded it.

claims.title: A pre-registered negative result: the simplest de-confounding recovered nothing
claims.statement: Subtracting each session's own batch benign median, with leave-one-out so a session never enters its own baseline, costs 0.0057 in Permissive and 0.0163 in Enforce; adding a scale step costs a further 0.0045 and 0.0715. The registered criterion asked for at least +0.05 and treated at most +0.01 as falsification, so both steps fail. Two of my own registered leakage checks turned out to have no discriminating power, for independent reasons, and one of them printed a passing tick in the mode where it was weakest. What is falsified is that specific de-confounding, not the broader claim that the information is recoverable.

claims.title: A pre-registered control caught my own reading of the long-scale drift
claims.statement: An earlier judgement that Enforce carries a long-timescale component beyond the batch effect was made without controlling for capture volume, and the per-epoch pcap medians differ by a factor of 36.19. After stratifying, both components survive: Spearman against volume gap is +0.6252 against +0.4205 for time gap, the two explanatory variables correlate at +0.4482 so they cannot be separated statistically, and within the most volume-matched layer the epoch effect is still 1.667, with 20 of 20 classes above 1.3. The structure is sharper than the magnitude: one epoch boundary shows no displacement and the next shows a large one, so it is not every configuration change.
